source_title: read/write switch2 save data through a ns2jb session. run lua inside lullaby without a switch 1. - GitHub
source_excerpt:
read, back up, restore and modify save data for any installed Switch 2 game over a live ns2jb session. the save path is not game-specific: it opens a title's save archive, moves files in or out, commits, and verifies by hash.
the same access is then used for one more thing: an Artemis save can be retargeted so the game resumes our Lua instead of its own script. that is the "save launch" half ( payloads/ , tools/artemis-save.py ); the save half works on any title you own.
the exploit is not here. nothing in this repo is exploit code, keys, or game content.
a patched ns2jb checkout (the local ~/ns2jb-rpc checkout, or run.cjs from ns2jb), an exploit session held open, and the run folder it prints ( runs/switch2-XXXXXX , containing switch2/ro/root/current-root.json ).
firmware 23.0.1 and SmileBASIC 4 (retail) to deliver the exploit.
the patch step is not optional; skip it only if the checkout already has the changes. docs/PATCHED-ENGINE.md explains what each patch fixes.
tools/kit.cjs adds no save logic of its own: it shells out to the proven scripts and prints the exact command before each one.
read-only by default; a write needs a prior backup and compares the live bytes against it before replacing anything;
only titles on the allowlist ( config/titles.json , plus your config/titles.local.json ) can be written;
one open, one commit, then every file is read back and hashed;
paths must be /name ; .. , nested paths and absolute paths are rejected.
several save operations per boot usually work; restart the console only if one actually fails. the one thing that reliably breaks the next session is leaving a previous one open ( --keep-open , a diagnostic only).
titles are listed from every storage ncm has a database for (internal, sd card, game card), and named from the console's own control data, not from a catalogue: that is the only way a switch 2 title gets a name. the name comes out of the title's control NCA (the read ouncecake falls back to; its ns reader did not answer on this console), so a japanese title can carry its japanese name. names are cached in config/titles.nacp.json ; --no-names skips the read.
is the 16-byte account uid in hex; --list-uids prints them. the pull prints mounted space=… type=… uid=… - read that line, it is how you learn that the right archive opened. docs/RESTORE.md covers the restore path and its limits; docs/SAVE-ARCHIVES.md covers which archive an open selects.
an Artemis slot save stores where execution resumes. retarget that pointer at save:/name.asb and the game resumes there; an ASB is a plain Lua container, so a few commands put our chunk in front of the engine. a second, zero-edit entry point is the suspend file: save_prefix="save" + save_suspend=9999 makes the game look for save9999.dat at boot.
docs/LAUNCHER.md - the chain, what is proven on hardware, what is blocked.
tools/build-untethered.sh - build the stub + body + suspend launcher from a backup; tools/inject-launcher.sh - backup, build, write, pull and verify.
the stub/body split is built and smoke-tested, not yet installed on hardware.
the controller/esp32 work lives in ns2-console ; the content/asset pipeline is in ns2-assets .
our code is MIT (see LICENSE ). third-party components and links are listed in NOTICE : ns2jb (the exploit, linked not vendored), Seedsow Lua Editor (0BSD; its save is downloaded, never bundled), titledb (MIT, names only), and the Artemis engine (no affiliation, no game content).
